name: grep
description: Search the workspace for lines matching a pattern, and report them as path:line:text. Use to find where a piece of text appears. To find files by name rather than by what is in them, use glob.

pattern.description: What to look for. A POSIX extended regular expression by default (so \\d and \\b are not available; use [0-9] and a word boundary of your own). Set fixed: true to search for it as literal text instead, which is what you want for anything containing . * [ ] ( ) | + ? ^ $ or \\.

path.description: Directory or single file to search, relative to the workspace root. Must resolve inside it. Defaults to the whole workspace.

glob.description: Only search files whose name matches this shell pattern, e.g. "*.py" or "*.test.js". It matches the file name, not the path, so "src/*.py" will match nothing.

fixed.description: Treat pattern as literal text rather than a regular expression.

max_matches.description: Stop after this many reported lines and say so. Raise it only when the truncated result was genuinely not enough.

output_schema.description: One match per line as "<path>:<line>:<text>". Paths are relative to the workspace root, so a result can be handed straight to read_file. A final "[grep] output truncated: ..." line is appended when max_matches was reached. Finding nothing is a successful search: the output is a single "[grep] no matches for ..." line and the exit code is 0.

exit_codes.0: success (the search ran; it found matches or it did not)
exit_codes.2: invalid input (stdin was not a JSON object, or a parameter is missing or the wrong type)
exit_codes.3: not found (the search path does not exist)
exit_codes.4: not permitted (the search path resolves outside the workspace root, or is not readable)
